_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES: idx 2, 4, 6. PAGE MAP (7 pages, p00-p06, matching the cover's 'Page 1 of 7' ... 'Page 7 of 7') — idx 0 bilingual cover · idx 1 Hindi instructions + Hindi Q1-Q4 · idx 2 English General Instructions + English Q1-Q4 · idx 3 Hindi Q5-Q10 · idx 4 English Q5-Q10 · idx 5 Hindi Q11-Q14 · idx 6 English Q11-Q14. The alternating hypothesis HELD with no exceptions. I started from contact.png (which answered the parity question in one look) and then confirmed at full size: idx 3 opens with the Hindi '5. मान ज्ञात कीजिए :' and idx 5 opens with the Hindi 'खण्ड ग' heading, so NEITHER odd page carries English overflow at its top — each English block ends flush at a question boundary and no question spans a language break. There is no parity inversion and no English-only final page: idx 6 is the last page and is English. All 14 question numbers present and unbroken. STRUCTURE, read off the printed General Instructions (idx 2): three sections, 14 questions, 40 marks, 2 hours; Section A Q1-6 @2 (12) + Section B Q7-10 @3 (12) + Section C Q11-13 @4 (12) + Q14 case study 2+2 (4) = 40. NO MCQs anywhere — every one of the 14 questions is subjective, so there are no options, no answer letters and no key to re-derive. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) reads 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO COUNTS, so the count was established by walking the OFFICIAL MARKING SCHEME question by question (ms idx 2-9, which reprints each stem and both branches wherever an OR exists) and cross-reading the printed 'OR' on the paper itself. FOUR internal choices — Q3, Q8, Q9, Q11 — and TEN questions with none (Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q10, Q12, Q13, Q14). Both branches ingested for all four. Row count 19 = 10 single + 4x2 alternatives + 1 case study x 2 sub-parts. OVERLAP WITH 65/4/1: 15 of the 19 rows are the same question, judged by CONTENT against data/2022-65-4-1.questions.json and confirmed on my own page before reuse; their stem/context text is reused BYTE-FOR-BYTE so they dedup at commit. The four genuinely NEW rows are Q6 (two bags), Q7 (area of y^2 <= x <= y), Q10 (|a+b|/|a-b| = cot(alpha/2)) and Q12 (integral of x/(9sin^2 x + 16cos^2 x)). plan.txt was WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS and was not followed: it claimed 8 shared / 5 new when the true split is 15 rows shared / 4 new, EVERY ONE of its eight block attributions names the wrong reference question (it says my Q1 = 65/4/1 Q1, but my Q1 is 65/4/1's Q3 — 65/4/1's Q1, the 3-red-4-white bag question, is not in this paper at all; likewise my Q2 = ref Q2 not ref Q3, my Q3 = ref Q4 not ref Q5, my Q13 = ref Q11 not ref Q11#1/Q13#1), and it listed Q7 as a SKIP when Q7 is genuinely new (65/4/1's Q7 is the region x^2 <= y <= x+2, a different region). Marking-scheme numbering equals paper numbering here — ms Q1 is the plane question, exactly as on the paper — so the mis-attribution is in plan.txt's block hashing, not a numbering offset. MARKING-SCHEME PRINTING SLIP: in the Marks column the scheme leaves Q7's entry BLANK, where every other question prints its mark value; the paper itself prints 3 against Q7 and the scheme's own 'Question Nos. 7 to 10 carry 3 marks each' header covers it, so nothing is ambiguous — noted only so a later reader does not read the blank as a missing question. Marking-scheme coverage verified complete: ms idx 0-1 are the evaluator's general instructions, idx 2-9 carry Q1/A1 through Q14/A14 with no question missing.

questions.stem: The foot of a perpendicular drawn from the point \((-2, -1, -3)\) on a plane is \((1, -3, 3)\). Find the equation of the plane.

A coin is tossed twice. The following table shows the probability distribution of number of tails :

| X | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P(X) | K | 6K | 9K |

(a) Find the value of K.

(b) Is the coin tossed biased or unbiased ? Justify your answer.
If \(|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}|^2 = 400\) and \(|\vec{b}| = 5\), then find the value of \(|\vec{a}|\).
Find all the possible vectors of magnitude \(5\sqrt{3}\) which are equally inclined to the coordinate axes.

Find the general solution of the differential equation

\(\sec^2 x \cdot \tan y \, dx + \sec^2 y \cdot \tan x \, dy = 0.\)

There are two bags. Bag I contains 1 red and 3 white balls, and Bag II contains 3 red and 5 white balls. A bag is selected at random and a ball is drawn from it. Find the probability that the ball so drawn is red in colour.

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: Using integration, find the area of the region \(\{(x, y) : y^2 \le x \le y\}\).

If a line makes \(60^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\) angles with the positive directions of x-axis and z-axis respectively, then find the angle that it makes with the positive direction of y-axis. Hence, write the direction cosines of the line.
questions._flag: OFFICIAL KEY IS INCOMPLETE (not wrong) — a finding for the solution-authoring step, not something to resolve here. This paper's own marking scheme (page idx 5) correctly derives \(m^2 = 1/4 \Rightarrow m = \pm 1/2\) and then reports only \(\theta = 60^\circ\) with direction cosines \(\langle 1/2, 1/2, 1/\sqrt{2} \rangle\), silently dropping the \(m = -1/2\) branch (angle \(120^\circ\), direction cosines \(\langle 1/2, -1/2, 1/\sqrt{2} \rangle\)), which the printed stem admits just as much. The identical omission was independently recorded on 65/4/1 Q10a, so it is CBSE's, reproduced across both sets of the series, not a one-off slip.

questions.stem: Check whether the lines \(\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4}\) and \(\dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = z\) are skew or not.

questions.subtopic: Definite Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem

questions.stem: If \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are two vectors of equal magnitude and \(\alpha\) is the angle between them, then prove that \(\dfrac{|\vec{a} + \vec{b}|}{|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|} = \cot\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)\).
Find the particular solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y + \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} = 0\), given that \(y(1) = 0\).

Find the general solution of the differential equation

\(x (y^3 + x^3) \, dy = (2y^4 + 5x^3 y) \, dx.\)

Find the equations of the planes passing through the line of intersection of the planes \(\vec{r} \cdot (\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) = 6\) and \(\vec{r} \cdot (3\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 4\hat{k}) = 0\), which are at a distance of 1 unit from the origin.

questions.context:
In a game of Archery, each ring of the Archery target is valued. The centremost ring is worth 10 points and rest of the rings are allotted points 9 to 1 in sequential order moving outwards.

Archer A is likely to earn 10 points with a probability of \(0{\cdot}8\) and Archer B is likely the earn 10 points with a probability of \(0{\cdot}9\).

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :

If both of them hit the Archery target, then find the probability that
questions.stem: exactly one of them earns 10 points.
questions._figure: DECORATIVE — the printed archery-target illustration (page idx 6) only labels the rings '1 point' to '10 points', which the passage already states in words. Both probabilities needed (0·8, 0·9) are in the stem text. Not attached.
questions._flag: PRINTED AS-IS: the passage reads 'Archer B is likely the earn 10 points' where 'to earn' is meant. Transcribed faithfully. This is CBSE's own typesetting error, not a render artefact — this paper's official marking scheme (page idx 9) reprints the passage with the identical wording, and 65/4/1 prints the same case study with the same error.
